name: Post-Mastectomy Rehabilitation
summary: Rehabilitation addresses shoulder mobility, strength, scar symptoms, posture, lymphedema risk and return to daily activity while coordinating with oncology care.

redFlags: New unilateral swelling suggesting DVT or acute lymphedema complication
firstSteps: Check wound status, shoulder ROM, pain, swelling and sensory symptoms.
Measure arm circumference/volume when lymphedema concern exists.
Begin gentle shoulder mobility and breathing.
selfCare: Progressive strength rather than long-term arm avoidance

stages.label: Start: assess and set up
stages.goal: Restore shoulder motion and strength while monitoring wound healing, pain and lymphedema risk.
do: Check wound status, shoulder ROM, pain, swelling and sensory symptoms.
Measure arm circumference/volume when lymphedema concern exists.
Begin gentle shoulder mobility and breathing.
moveOn: Baseline recorded: Arm circumference/volume when indicated

stages.label: Treat: build capacity
stages.goal: Progress arm use rather than promoting long-term fear of lifting.
dose: Assisted shoulder flexion/abduction: 5–10 reps, several times/day early.
Progressive resistance: 2–3 sets × 8–15 reps once healing allows.
Aerobic activity: gradual return to regular walking/cycling.
moveOn: Return to work, lifting and recreation according to tolerance

stages.label: Progress and self-manage
stages.goal: Manual lymphatic drainage is specialized and only one part of lymphedema care.
when: Return to work, lifting and recreation according to tolerance
do: Progressive strength rather than long-term arm avoidance
dose: Increase overhead range and resistance slowly.
Progress lifting based on symptom/swelling response.

escalation: Medical review for cellulitis, rapid swelling, wound problems or suspected recurrence/other medical complication
